text: On QNX 8.0, qsentry caught a stuck sensor in half a second. In simulated drives it found all 800 faults, with no false alarms.
Brakes and stability control trust their sensors. A frozen or drifting sensor feeds them wrong numbers.
A sensor process sends every sample to qsentry with QNX message passing. A tiny neural network checks each sensor, and a timer pulse is the watchdog.
A real QNX 8.0 target in QEMU. Everything shown comes from its log.
Clean driving. Four signals at one hundred hertz, and every sensor is checked on every tick. State: nominal.
Now the gyro drifts. On its own it looks normal, but it no longer matches steering and speed. Flagged as drift after 2.79 seconds. Degraded.
The fault is cleared. A sensor is trusted again only after a full second of confident health. Back to nominal.
The wheel speed sensor freezes. Stuck, detected in 0.48 seconds. The gyro is not blamed by mistake.
Accelerometer noise, found in 0.18 seconds, plus gyro drift. Both redundant pairs are lost, so qsentry latches safe stop.
An operator reset while the window still holds faulty samples: safe stop latches again. qsentry never trusts stale evidence.
Two low priority programs load the CPU. The detector runs at priority forty and stays bounded: a median of 144 microseconds.
The sensor process is killed. A timer pulse on the same QNX channel is the watchdog: safe stop 55 milliseconds after the last sample.
On QNX: drift in 2.8 seconds, stuck sensor in 0.48, noise in 0.18, watchdog in 55 milliseconds.
qsentry is open source, Apache 2.0. The data is simulated: retrain on real data first.
